speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: The history of a preceding knee episode, recent camping in Minnesota, and now wrist pain with fever strongly suggests Lyme arthritis or early disseminated Lyme disease. Have you noticed a "bull's-eye" rash, or "Erythema Migrans," anywhere on your body, and do you recall being bitten by a tick? REQUEST IMAGES: Please provide photos of any skin rashes, specifically looking for a target-like lesion.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Lyme Arthritis with secondary cellulitis. The presentation of fever, wrist swelling, and erythema following a knee episode and camping in Minnesota is highly characteristic of Lyme disease, while the violaceous vesiculopustular lesions likely represent a secondary bacterial superinfection of the arthritic joint.
